nded3ca79b37.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the pocket veto of the President of India?
o: Under it, the President neither assents to, nor rejects, nor returns the Bill.
It is possible because Article 111 prescribes no time limit for the President's decision on a Bill.
As in the USA, the President must decide within 10 days, failing which the Bill becomes law.
President Giani Zail Singh used it on the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill, 1986.
nded3ca79b37.x: The 10-day limit is a US feature; Article 111 sets no time limit in India, which is what makes the pocket veto possible.

nindian-polity-74-19.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ordinances?
o: The President can withdraw an ordinance at any time.
The Governor can withdraw an ordinance at any time.
Re-promulgation without legislative ratification may subvert the Constitution.
The ordinance-making power is beyond judicial review.
nindian-polity-74-19.x: Ordinances are subject to judicial review; the other three statements are correct.

nindian-polity-74-34.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 13(2) – an ordinance abridging Part III rights is void
Article 368 – amendment power not available through an ordinance
nindian-polity-74-34.x: The Krishna Kumar Singh case was decided in 2017; 1987 is the D.C. Wadhwa case, which condemned repeated re-promulgation in Bihar.

nindian-polity-74-10.s:
Assertion (A): An ordinance can amend an ordinary Act and can be given retrospective effect.
Reason (R): An ordinance can be used to amend the Constitution under Article 368.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nindian-polity-74-10.x: Within legislative competence an ordinance can amend an ordinary Act, operate retrospectively and change taxes, but it cannot amend the Constitution under Article 368.

n3a40c5183af.s: Which of the following Bills can the President NOT return for reconsideration?
n3a40c5183af.x: Assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill is mandatory, so it cannot be returned; the one-time return power can apply to Financial Bills of Categories I and II.

ndd3eb77d5fd.s: In which case (2017) did the Supreme Court hold that re-promulgation of an Ordinance may be a fraud on the Constitution?
o: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Krishna Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar
A.K. Roy v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
ndd3eb77d5fd.x: Krishna Kumar Singh (2017) held that re-promulgation can be a fraud on the Constitution and that laying the Ordinance before the legislature is mandatory.

nindian-polity-74-28.s: Which Article fixes the maximum gap of six months between two sessions of Parliament?
nindian-polity-74-28.x: Article 85 sets the six-month limit for Parliament; Article 174 does the same for State Legislatures.

nindian-polity-74-12.s: If the two Houses reassemble on different dates, the six-week life of an ordinance is counted from:
o: the earlier of the two dates
the later of the two dates
the date the Rajya Sabha reassembles
nindian-polity-74-12.x: An ordinance must be laid before the legislature on reassembly, and if the Houses meet on different dates the six weeks run from the later date.

nindian-polity-74-3.s: An ordinance can be promulgated only when:
o: a Proclamation of Emergency is in force
the Lok Sabha passes a resolution permitting it
both Houses are in full session
nindian-polity-74-3.x: An ordinance can be issued only when the legislature is in recess and the Head of State is satisfied that immediate action is needed; none can be issued while both Houses are sitting.

nindian-polity-21-31.s: Which President exercised a pocket veto over the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill, 1986?
nindian-polity-21-31.x: Giani Zail Singh used a pocket veto on the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill, 1986.

nindian-polity-74-26.s: Under which Article is an ordinance treated as 'law', so that it is void if it abridges Fundamental Rights?
nindian-polity-74-26.x: An ordinance is 'law' under Article 13(2) and is void if it abridges Fundamental Rights, though it can make or change tax provisions within legislative power.

nindian-polity-7-13.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the duties of the Prime Minister towards the President?
o: The PM communicates to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers.
The PM furnishes information sought by the President.
The PM submits a Minister's decision for the Council's consideration when the President so requires.
These duties are laid down in Article 74.
nindian-polity-7-13.x: These duties of the PM are laid down in Article 78; Article 74 provides for the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President.

n46a5e3896bb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the categories of Union Ministers?
o: A Cabinet Minister heads an important ministry and attends Cabinet meetings.
A Deputy Minister heads an important ministry and attends Cabinet meetings.
A Minister of State with independent charge holds a ministry on his or her own.
A Minister of State is attached to a Cabinet Minister.
n46a5e3896bb.x: A Deputy Minister only assists a senior Minister; it is the Cabinet Minister who heads an important ministry and attends Cabinet meetings.

n41c47e78c3b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the size of a State Council of Ministers under Article 164(1A)?
o: Ministers, including the CM, cannot exceed 15% of the Assembly's strength.
The number of ministers cannot be less than 12.
The limit was inserted by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.
In a 294-member Assembly the maximum, including the CM, is 45.
n41c47e78c3b.x: 15% of 294 is 44.1, so the maximum is 44 (e.g. West Bengal), not 45.

n82eeaab72fd.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the removal of the Vice-President of India?
o: The resolution must originate in the Rajya Sabha.
The resolution needs a majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha.
The Lok Sabha must agree to the resolution by a simple majority.
The Constitution specifies the grounds for removal.
n82eeaab72fd.x: The Constitution does not state any grounds for removing the Vice-President; the other three statements describe the procedure correctly.

n74969792cf4.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates)
n74969792cf4.s: Which Article provides that the advice tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into by any court?
n74969792cf4.x: Article 74(2) bars courts from inquiring into ministerial advice; Article 77 deals with executive action in the President's name, authentication of orders and business rules.

ne026ef296d1.s: Who was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India?
ne026ef296d1.x: Sardar Patel was the first Deputy PM; the office is not mentioned in the Constitution and its holder takes oath as an ordinary Minister.

nindian-polity-7-18.s: Who was the first non-Congress Prime Minister of India?
nindian-polity-7-18.x: Morarji Desai was the first non-Congress Prime Minister of India.

n886da302b8c.s: Who was the first acting Prime Minister of India (in 1964 and 1966)?
n886da302b8c.x: Gulzarilal Nanda was the first acting Prime Minister, in 1964 and again in 1966.

nindian-polity-9-10.s: The office of the Vice-President of India is modelled on that of the:
o: Deputy Prime Minister of the UK
nindian-polity-9-10.x: The Indian Vice-President's office is modelled on the American Vice-President.

nd7d19c8cde7.s: The Vice-President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of:
o: elected members of both Houses of Parliament only
elected MPs and elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies
all members of both Houses of Parliament, elected and nominated
all MPs and elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies
nd7d19c8cde7.x: All MPs, elected and nominated, vote by PR-STV and secret ballot; State legislatures have no role in the Vice-President's election.

nindian-polity-46-20.s: Which body is the core decision-making body of the Union Government?
nindian-polity-46-20.x: The Union Cabinet, the top tier of the ministerial hierarchy, is the core decision-making body, not the whole Council of Ministers.

n01536151771.s: Under the 130th Constitution Amendment Bill, 2025, a Minister detained for 30 consecutive days for an offence punishable with five or more years would be removed on the:
n01536151771.x: The Bill provides for removal on the 31st day after 30 consecutive days of detention; it touches Articles 75, 164 and 239AA.

na87818cb0dd.s: The classification of Union Ministers into different ranks is based on:
o: convention and the choice of the Prime Minister
the Third Schedule of the Constitution
na87818cb0dd.x: The Constitution does not classify ministers into ranks; the ranks, including Deputy Minister, rest on convention and the PM's choice.

nindian-polity-46-33.s: Which Article gives Ministers the right to speak in both Houses of Parliament?
nindian-polity-46-33.x: Article 88 gives Ministers the right to speak in both Houses; 75(2) is pleasure tenure, 75(3) collective responsibility and 75(5) the six-month rule.

nd2685d9f94f.s: Who administers the oath of office to the Vice-President of India?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The senior-most judge of the Supreme Court
nd2685d9f94f.x: Under Article 69 the President administers the Vice-President's oath; the CJI administers the President's oath.

o: the PM and Cabinet-rank Ministers only
the PM, Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers
the PM and Ministers of State only
the PM, Cabinet Ministers and Deputy Ministers
nindian-polity-46-10.x: The Cabinet (about 15–20) is the PM and Cabinet-rank Ministers; the wider Council (about 60–80) also includes Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers.

nindian-polity-56-9.s: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha addresses his resignation to the:
o: Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha
nindian-polity-56-9.x: Under Article 94 the Speaker resigns to the Deputy Speaker.

n92b6c7abbe5.s: A non-member appointed as a Union Minister must become a member of either House of Parliament within:
n92b6c7abbe5.x: The six-month rule applies to every non-member Minister, including the Prime Minister.

nindian-polity-7-6.s: Which Article provides for a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President?
nindian-polity-7-6.x: Article 74 provides for the Council of Ministers to aid and advise; Article 75 covers appointment and tenure, and Article 78 the PM's duties.

nindian-polity-9-18.s: Who was the first President of India to die in office?
nindian-polity-9-18.x: Dr Zakir Husain was the first President to die in office; V.V. Giri then acted as President in 1969.

nindian-polity-46-6.s: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
nindian-polity-46-6.x: The Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

n2adab80b6eb.s: When Manmohan Singh, a Rajya Sabha member, was Prime Minister, who was named Leader of the House in the Lok Sabha?
n2adab80b6eb.x: The Leader of the House is not a constitutional office; a PM who is not a Lok Sabha member nominates a minister, and Pranab Mukherjee was named under Manmohan Singh.

n5fa1681944b.s: P.V. Narasimha Rao, who became Prime Minister in 1991 without being an MP, later entered the Lok Sabha from:
n5fa1681944b.x: Narasimha Rao, the first PM from South India, entered the Lok Sabha from Nandyal.

nindian-polity-9-5.s: Which Article makes the Vice-President the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
nindian-polity-9-5.x: Article 64 makes the Vice-President ex-officio Chairman; 63 creates the office, 66 covers election and 67 the term.

nindian-polity-56-2.s: To whom does the Governor of a State address his resignation?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
nindian-polity-56-2.x: The Governor resigns to the President; the High Court's Chief Justice administers his oath.

nbd051a62ffe.s: Which of the following pairs of Cabinet Committee and its concern is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Cabinet Committee on Security – Defence, national security and nuclear doctrine
Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs – Economic and infrastructure projects
Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs – Senior appointments
nbd051a62ffe.x: Senior appointments are the concern of the Appointments Committee; the Parliamentary Affairs Committee deals with government business and parliamentary sessions.

n10d8744bf8f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Department of Personnel?
o: It originated from the Administrative Reforms Commission of 1966.
It was placed under the Prime Minister.
The N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar report recommended it to provide a minister and secretary solely for administrative reform.
n10d8744bf8f.x: The Ayyangar report did not suggest a minister and secretary solely for administrative reform; the Department came in 1970 out of the 1966 ARC and was placed under the PM.

n785a464778b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Attorney General of India?
o: The office is not a full-time office.
The Attorney General may take up private practice.
The Attorney General may advise or brief against the Government of India.
The Attorney General cannot become a company director without permission.
n785a464778b.x: Though private practice is permitted, the Attorney General cannot advise or brief against the Government of India.

nc3014f731d8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Cabinet Committees?
o: The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs handles Centre-State and political issues.
The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs is described as a 'super cabinet'.
The decision on caste enumeration in the Census was taken by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.
The Committees on Investment and Growth and on Employment and Skill Development were set up in 2019.
nc3014f731d8.x: Caste enumeration in the Census was decided by the Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs, not the CCEA.

nindian-polity-31-14.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Advocate General of a State is appointed by the Governor.
The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
The Advocate General of a State is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet.
The Solicitor General's term is fixed at appointment, usually three years.
nindian-polity-31-14.x: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet appoints the Solicitor General of India; the Advocate General is appointed by the Governor.

ne02e6d090e6.s: Which body generally meets regularly and takes the policy decisions of the Union Government?
o: The Council of Ministers as a whole
ne02e6d090e6.x: The wider Council of Ministers (Articles 74 and 75) rarely meets as a body; the Cabinet meets regularly and takes policy decisions.

nindian-polity-31-10.s: Who is the highest law officer of the Government of India?
nindian-polity-31-10.x: The Attorney General is India's highest law officer; the Solicitor General assists the Attorney General.

n2de13198db5.s: Which of the following Cabinet Committees is NOT chaired by the Prime Minister?
n2de13198db5.x: The Accommodation Committee is chaired by a senior minister; the PM chairs the Appointments, Security and Political Affairs Committees.

nfcc87391c51.s: A no-confidence motion against the Union Council of Ministers can be moved in:
o: a joint sitting of both Houses
nfcc87391c51.x: Under Article 75(3) the Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, so a no-confidence motion lies only there; even Rajya Sabha ministers are responsible to the Lok Sabha.

ne3e5d9379c8.s: Which of the following does NOT, by itself, require the whole Union ministry to resign?
o: Passage of a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha
Defeat on a money bill in the Lok Sabha
Defeat of the Government in the Rajya Sabha
Defeat on a major policy measure in the Lok Sabha
ne3e5d9379c8.x: Only loss of Lok Sabha confidence can lead the ministry to resign; defeat in the Rajya Sabha does not by itself compel resignation.

n035b588a334.s: The existence of nominal and real executives is a feature of the:
n035b588a334.x: Nominal and real executives and dissolution of the lower House are parliamentary features; separation of powers marks the presidential system.

o: The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs
The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet
nd1e55b22f93.x: The ACC appoints the Cabinet Secretary, the senior-most civil servant, for two years extendable up to four.

n2d871a6489d.s: The word 'Cabinet' was inserted into Article 352 of the Constitution by the:
n2d871a6489d.x: The 44th Amendment, 1978 inserted it; Article 352(3) is the only place the word 'Cabinet' appears.

n43bd5c2ad15.s: In which year were the existing Groups of Ministers (GoMs) and Empowered GoMs abolished?
n43bd5c2ad15.x: The existing GoMs and EGoMs, criticised for delay and diluting collective responsibility, were abolished in 2014.

n84497b50ecd.s: Experience under which Acts influenced India's adoption of the parliamentary form of government?
o: Government of India Acts of 1919 and 1935
Regulating Act of 1773 and Pitt's India Act of 1784
n84497b50ecd.x: India chose the parliamentary form because of experience under the Acts of 1919 and 1935 and to avoid a personality cult.

n56ad280a58b.s: Who heads the National Crisis Management Committee?
n56ad280a58b.x: The Cabinet Secretary, first among equals among Secretaries and eleventh in the Table of Precedence, heads the NCMC.

n0f4df986727.s: Which of the following is a necessary feature of the parliamentary form of government in India?
o: Complete separation of the executive from the legislature
n0f4df986727.x: Majority party rule, collective responsibility and the PM as the centre of power are its necessary features; complete separation of powers belongs to the presidential system.

ne509ae39309.s: The Cabinet Secretariat functions directly under the:
ne509ae39309.x: The Cabinet Secretariat, which serves the Cabinet and its committees and administers the Business Rules, functions directly under the PM.

nfcdbe4ab161.s: The N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar report on the reorganisation of the machinery of government dates from:
nfcdbe4ab161.x: The 1949 Ayyangar report dealt with reorganising the machinery of government, including grouping of ministries and Cabinet Committees.

nc219f4229f9.s: Comparing the Rajya Sabha and the US Senate, which pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Rajya Sabha – election by elected MLAs through PR-STV
nc219f4229f9.x: The US Senate has no nominated members; the Rajya Sabha has 12.

n14db45eda9f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Speaker certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill.
The Rajya Sabha can initiate a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers.
The Speaker presides over a joint sitting of Parliament.
The Rajya Sabha has no vote on Demands for Grants.
n14db45eda9f.x: A no-confidence motion is a device of the Lok Sabha alone, not the Rajya Sabha.

nf23467a1f86.s:
Assertion (A): The Governor is a part of both unicameral and bicameral State Legislatures.
Reason (R): Provisions on State Legislatures are contained in Part VI, Articles 168 to 212.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nf23467a1f86.x: A unicameral legislature is Governor + Assembly and a bicameral one is Governor + Assembly + Council; R is a true statement about where the provisions lie but does not explain A.

nb40c7604217.s: The minimum strength of a State Legislative Council is:
nb40c7604217.x: A Legislative Council must have at least 40 members and cannot exceed one-third of the Assembly's strength.

naa1a494fdcb.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Parliament of India?
naa1a494fdcb.x: Parliament consists of the President, the Council of States and the House of the People; State Legislative Councils are not part of it.

nef83f733b0e.s: Within how many days must the Rajya Sabha return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha?
nef83f733b0e.x: A Money Bill must be returned within 14 days, showing the Rajya Sabha is weaker than the Lok Sabha in financial matters.

n8fce548c6c7.s: Israel's unicameral national legislature is called the:
n8fce548c6c7.x: Israel, like China, New Zealand, Sweden and Denmark, has a unicameral legislature; it is the Knesset.

nindian-polity-45-3.s: Which Article provides for the Council of Ministers in a State?
nindian-polity-45-3.x: Article 163 covers the State Council of Ministers; Article 74 the Union Council, Article 80 the Council of States and Articles 168, 169 and 171 the Legislative Council.

n7881026a795.s: Besides its 30 elected members, the Puducherry Assembly can have:
n7881026a795.x: Puducherry has 30 elected members and up to 3 nominated members; Delhi has 70 seats and Jammu and Kashmir 90 elected seats.

nc6c1f520bae.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about disqualification on the ground of defection?
o: A member who voluntarily gives up membership of his party is liable to disqualification.
An independent member who joins a party after election is liable to disqualification.
A nominated member who joins a party after six months from taking his seat is liable to disqualification.
The President decides every question of disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.
nc6c1f520bae.x: Under the Tenth Schedule the Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha decides such questions, subject to judicial review.

na782ceb2ac0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the President as a component of Parliament?
o: The President is a part of Parliament but not a member of either House.
No Bill passed by Parliament becomes law without the President's assent.
The President sits in Parliament as a member while addressing the Houses.
The President summons and prorogues the Houses of Parliament.
na782ceb2ac0.x: The President is a component of Parliament but never sits as a member of either House.

n42655f5dbae.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026?
o: It was introduced along with the Delimitation Bill, 2026.
It sought to raise the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850.
The proposed 850 seats comprised 815 for the States and 35 for the Union Territories.
It was passed by the Lok Sabha with the required special majority.
n42655f5dbae.x: The Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha and so did not secure the required special majority.

n4eecb9ef37b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about women's reservation under the 106th Constitutional Amendment?
o: It applies to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
It reserves one-half of the seats in these legislatures.
Its operation is governed by Article 334A.
It is initially meant to operate for fifteen years and may be extended.
n4eecb9ef37b.x: The 106th Amendment reserves one-third of the seats, not one-half.

nf7d7d0b257d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about vacation of seats under Article 101?
o: If a sitting member of one House is elected to the other, his seat in the first House falls vacant.
If a person elected to two seats in the same House does not choose one, both seats fall vacant.
If a person elected to both Houses does not choose within 10 days, his Lok Sabha seat falls vacant.
A House may declare a seat vacant if a member is absent without permission for 60 days.
nf7d7d0b257d.x: In that case it is the Rajya Sabha seat that falls vacant, not the Lok Sabha seat.

n8fdf33ff085.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sita Soren case (2024)?
o: It was decided by a seven-judge Bench.
It held that privilege does not protect a legislator who takes a bribe to vote or speak.
It overruled the protection recognised in P.V. Narasimha Rao (1998) on this point.
It held that every speech made by a legislator outside the House is protected by Article 105.
n8fdf33ff085.x: Sita Soren held no such thing; it held that parliamentary privilege does not protect bribery for voting or speaking.

n890ab4fb617.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019?
o: It discontinued the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha.
The discontinuance took effect from 25 January 2020.
It ended the reservation of Lok Sabha seats for SCs and STs.
Before it, Article 331 enabled the President to nominate up to two Anglo-Indians.
n890ab4fb617.x: The 104th Amendment extended SC/ST reservation by ten years, till 2030; it ended only Anglo-Indian nomination.

n8fdaa1d2256.s: On which of the following matters do the two Houses of Parliament NOT have equal powers?
o: Removal of a Judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court
Approval of an Ordinance promulgated by the President
Passing a resolution to discontinue a National Emergency
n8fdaa1d2256.x: Only the Lok Sabha can pass a resolution to discontinue a National Emergency; the Houses are equal on the other three.

n782f0d49163.s:
Assertion (A): The Speaker may refuse to accept a member's written resignation.
Reason (R): A resignation may be rejected if the presiding officer is satisfied that it is not voluntary or genuine.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n782f0d49163.x: A resignation is addressed in writing to the Speaker or Chairman, and it can be rejected precisely because it is found not voluntary or genuine, so R explains A.

n9f358e61db5.s: The representatives of a State in the Rajya Sabha are elected by:
o: all members of the State Legislative Assembly, including nominated members
the elected members of the State Legislative Assembly
the elected members of both Houses of the State Legislature
the people of the State directly
n9f358e61db5.x: Under Article 80(4) they are elected by the elected MLAs through PR-STV; nominated MLAs do not take part.

nindian-polity-44-4.s: Which Article deals with the procedure for impeachment of the President?
nindian-polity-44-4.x: Impeachment is under Article 61; Article 109 covers the Rajya Sabha's 14 days on Money Bills and 90(c) the Deputy Chairman's removal.

n27efb90d04a.s: Which of the following is NOT a field listed in Article 80(3) for nomination to the Rajya Sabha?
n27efb90d04a.x: Article 80(3) lists literature, science, art and social service; sports is not among them.

n21ab69350f2.s: Under which Article can the Rajya Sabha authorise the creation of new All-India Services?
n21ab69350f2.x: Article 312 covers new All-India Services; 249 deals with State List legislation in the national interest and 67(b) with initiating the Vice-President's removal.

nindian-polity-39-9.s: Which is the second-largest Lok Sabha constituency by geographical area?
nindian-polity-39-9.x: Ladakh is the largest, Barmer the second-largest and Kachchh the third; Chandni Chowk is the smallest.

nffa4bf616b2.s: Which Article protects the freedom of speech of members in Parliament?
nffa4bf616b2.x: Article 105 bars court proceedings for anything said or any vote given in Parliament or its committees; it does not cover statements made outside.

nindian-polity-13-19.s: Who was the first film actress nominated to the Rajya Sabha (1980)?
nindian-polity-13-19.x: Nargis Dutt, nominated in 1980, was the first film actress in the Rajya Sabha.

n43599e6a690.s: A Bill under Article 3 to form a new State can be introduced in Parliament only on the recommendation of the:
n43599e6a690.x: Such a Bill needs the President's recommendation; the State Legislature's views are sought but are not binding on Parliament.

n13fdea688b7.s: During a National Emergency, the term of the Lok Sabha can be extended by law for:
n13fdea688b7.x: The term can be extended one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ends.

n4a6d1144a8a.s: Which of the following is a judicial function of Parliament?
n4a6d1144a8a.x: Impeachment of the President, removal of the Vice-President, recommending removal of judges and punishing breach of privilege are Parliament's judicial functions.

nac312301d57.s: A Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 must be supported by:
o: two-thirds of members present and voting
a simple majority of members present and voting
a majority of the total membership
nac312301d57.x: It needs two-thirds of members present and voting, is valid for one year and can be renewed one year at a time.

n28a0fe76ad3.s: Which Article allows the business of Parliament to be transacted in Hindi or English?
n28a0fe76ad3.x: Article 120 recognises Hindi and English and lets a member use his mother tongue with the presiding officer's permission.

ndf570beef46.s: In which case (2006) did the Supreme Court uphold the open ballot and the removal of the domicile requirement for Rajya Sabha elections?
o: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India
Sita Soren v. Union of India
Krishna Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar
ndf570beef46.x: Kuldip Nayar (2006) upheld both the removal of the domicile requirement and the open-ballot system.

nindian-polity-38-26.s: Termination of a session of a House, without ending the life of the House, is called:
nindian-polity-38-26.x: Prorogation ends the session; adjournment ends a sitting for a set time, adjournment sine die ends it without a date, and dissolution ends the House.

neae7fbebb7c.s: The minimum age for membership of the Rajya Sabha is:
neae7fbebb7c.x: The minimum age is 30 for the Rajya Sabha and 25 for the Lok Sabha; no educational qualification is prescribed.

nd57bd0502b1.s: Under the proposal to enlarge the Lok Sabha by about 50% once the 1971 freeze lifts, its strength would rise to about:
nd57bd0502b1.x: The House would grow to about 815, and the 15% ministerial ceiling would rise from 81 to 122 (133 by another source).

n928374dd039.s: Nominated members of the Rajya Sabha can vote in the election of the:
o: both the President and the Vice-President
neither the President nor the Vice-President
n928374dd039.x: Nominated members vote in the Vice-Presidential election but not in the Presidential election.

nindian-polity-12-13.s: What was the elected strength of the First Lok Sabha?
nindian-polity-12-13.x: The First Lok Sabha had 489 elected seats; the present elected strength is 543.

nf1def5a64e7.s: Besides members, parliamentary privileges also extend to the:
nf1def5a64e7.x: Privileges extend to ministers, the Attorney-General and others who speak in the House; the House also has collective privileges.

n85bee2a9317.s: An existing law made by Parliament can be changed only by:
n85bee2a9317.x: Only Parliament can change an existing law it has made (APPSC-GS 2024); it legislates on the Union and Concurrent Lists and reviews delegated legislation.

nf2794f45b9d.s: The President dissolves the Lok Sabha before its term on the advice of the:
nf2794f45b9d.x: Early dissolution is on the PM's advice, not the Speaker's, and cannot be challenged in court; the five-year term runs from the first meeting (Art. 83(2)).

nindian-polity-2-42.s: Which Article deals with the composition of the Lok Sabha?
nindian-polity-2-42.x: Article 81 covers the Lok Sabha; 79 the constitution of Parliament, 80 the Rajya Sabha and 83 the duration of the Houses.

n67f6017a070.s: No tax can be imposed without the approval of the:
n67f6017a070.x: No tax can be levied without Lok Sabha approval; questions and motions are other tools of control over the executive.

n71d762870e8.s: Seats in the Rajya Sabha are allotted to the States under the:
n71d762870e8.x: Seats are allotted by population under the Fourth Schedule (Arts. 4 and 80(2)), not equally as in the US Senate; UP has the most (31).

nindian-polity-45-11.s: The maximum sanctioned strength of the Rajya Sabha is:
nindian-polity-45-11.x: The maximum is 250: 238 from States and UTs and 12 nominated members.

nindian-polity-78-15.s: Which Article provides for elections on the basis of universal adult suffrage?
nindian-polity-78-15.x: Adult suffrage is under Article 326; Article 84(b) deals with Lok Sabha membership.

n069a4ff84b7.s: How many Lok Sabha seats does Telangana have?
n069a4ff84b7.x: Telangana has 17 Lok Sabha seats; Andhra Pradesh has 25 and Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir 5 each.

nd059d983a0d.s: How many Rajya Sabha seats does Andhra Pradesh have?
nd059d983a0d.x: Andhra Pradesh has 11 Rajya Sabha seats; Telangana has 7, Uttarakhand 3 and Tripura 1.

nb2379103d1e.s: In which year was the first Women's Reservation Bill introduced?
nb2379103d1e.x: The first Bill came in 1996 and was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010; the 106th Amendment was enacted in 2023.

n71ae71792ca.s: In which year was Sachin Tendulkar nominated to the Rajya Sabha?
n71ae71792ca.x: Sachin Tendulkar was nominated in 2012 and Mary Kom in 2016.

nd72053ba9a5.s: The right to be informed of a member's arrest, detention or release is:
o: an individual privilege of the member
a Fundamental Right of the member under Article 22
a collective privilege of the House
a privilege of the Presiding Officer alone
nd72053ba9a5.x: Being informed of a member's arrest, detention or release is a collective privilege of the House.

ndd272db4da4.s: How many Lok Sabha seats does Tripura have?
ndd272db4da4.x: Tripura has 2 Lok Sabha seats (and one Rajya Sabha seat); Sikkim, Mizoram and Nagaland have one Lok Sabha seat each.

n2003beefe86.s: Under Article 87, the President makes a special address to both Houses at the commencement of:
o: the first session after each general election and the first session of each year
only the first session after each general election
only the first session of each year
n2003beefe86.x: The Article 87 special address is made at the first session after each general election and the first session of each year; Article 86 is the general power to address either or both Houses.

o: a permanent House not subject to dissolution
dissolved along with the Lok Sabha
dissolved by the President on the PM's advice
n2414d16c71e.x: The Rajya Sabha is permanent and never dissolved; its members retire by rotation.

ne6d05edbb8c.s: Which Article provides for the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
ne6d05edbb8c.x: Article 89(2) provides for the Deputy Chairman, chosen from among Rajya Sabha members; the Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman under Articles 64 and 89(1), and Article 93 is the Lok Sabha Speaker.

nindian-polity-78-29.s: Which Article lays down the minimum age qualification for the Governor of a State?
nindian-polity-78-29.x: Article 157 covers the Governor; 58(1)(b) the President, 66(3)(b) the Vice-President and 84(b) members of Parliament.

nindian-polity-12-11.s: Reservation of Lok Sabha seats for SCs and STs was initially provided for:
nindian-polity-12-11.x: Seats are reserved for SCs and STs in proportion to their population; the reservation was first given for ten years.

nindian-polity-2-44.s: Which Article deals with Appropriation Bills?
nindian-polity-2-44.x: Article 114 covers Appropriation Bills; 100 is voting and quorum, 105 privileges and 113 the procedure for estimates.

nindian-polity-13-12.s: What proportion of Rajya Sabha members retire every two years?
nindian-polity-13-12.x: A member serves six years and about one-third retire every two years; a casual vacancy is filled only for the rest of the term.

nindian-polity-36-32.s: Who among the following can vote in Rajya Sabha elections?
nindian-polity-36-32.x: Rajya Sabha elections are indirect, by elected MLAs; nominated MLAs and MLCs cannot vote.

nindian-polity-13-14.s: The powers of the Rajya Sabha are restricted in the case of:
nindian-polity-13-14.x: The Rajya Sabha has equal powers on Constitutional Amendment Bills and can introduce Ordinary and Amendment Bills; it is restricted only for Money Bills.

ncbeb2036508.s: Regarding the first Andhra Pradesh Legislature, which pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Speaker of the first Assembly – Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao
Deputy Speaker of the first Assembly – Kalluri Subbarao
First Chairman of the Legislative Council – Kalluri Subbarao
ncbeb2036508.x: The first Council Chairman was Madapati Hanumantha Rao; Kalluri Subbarao was the Deputy Speaker.

nb4c56bdbfb2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
o: The Deputy Speaker is elected after the election of the Speaker.
The Deputy Speaker resigns by writing to the Speaker.
The Deputy Speaker presides over a joint sitting when the Speaker is absent.
The Deputy Speaker is subordinate to the Speaker in exercising the office's functions.
nb4c56bdbfb2.x: The Deputy Speaker is not subordinate to the Speaker while exercising the functions of the office.

n86bba541116.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the powers of the Speaker?
o: The Speaker recognises the Leader of the Opposition, subject to the party-strength requirement.
The Speaker's decisions under the Tenth Schedule are beyond judicial review.
The Speaker appoints chairmen of parliamentary committees.
Rulings of the Speaker are protected by Article 122.
n86bba541116.x: The Speaker decides Tenth Schedule cases, but those decisions remain subject to judicial review.

n690f2a8fefa.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Secretary-General of a House of Parliament?
o: Each House has a Secretary-General as head of its secretarial staff.
The Secretary-General holds rank equal to the Cabinet Secretary.
The parliamentary secretariat is independent of the executive.
The Secretary-General is appointed by the Union Government.
n690f2a8fefa.x: The Secretary-General is appointed by the presiding officer of the House concerned, keeping the secretariat independent of the executive.

nindian-polity-58-20.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Deputy Speaker's resignation – addressed to the Speaker
Speaker's resignation – addressed to the President
Removal of the Speaker or Deputy Speaker – effective majority after 14 days' notice
Speaker's office on dissolution – continues until just before the new House first meets
nindian-polity-58-20.x: The Speaker resigns to the Deputy Speaker, not to the President.

nindian-polity-57-17.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Regular Speaker – elected by Lok Sabha members
Pro-Tem Speaker – elected by Lok Sabha members
nindian-polity-57-17.x: The Pro-Tem Speaker is appointed by the President under Article 95(1); only the regular Speaker is elected by the House.

nindian-polity-64-8.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Adjournment – Presiding Officer, suspending a sitting for a specified time
Adjournment sine die – Presiding Officer, without naming a day of reassembly
nindian-polity-64-8.x: The President prorogues under Article 85(2)(a); Article 85(2)(b) is dissolution.

nindian-polity-58-16.s:
Assertion (A): Unlike the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker vacates office at once when the Lok Sabha is dissolved.
Reason (R): Both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nindian-polity-58-16.x: Only the Speaker stays in office after dissolution; election by the House is a feature common to both, so it cannot explain the difference in A.

nindian-polity-64-7.s:
Assertion (A): Prorogation ends the very life of the Lok Sabha.
Reason (R): Adjournment suspends the work in a sitting for a specified time.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nindian-polity-64-7.x: Prorogation only ends a session; it is dissolution that ends the Lok Sabha itself. R correctly describes adjournment.

nca3fe95b268.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates)
nca3fe95b268.s: When the Vice-President acts as President, the duties of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha are performed by the:
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
senior-most member of the Rajya Sabha
Leader of the House in the Rajya Sabha
nca3fe95b268.x: The Deputy Chairman performs the Chairman's duties when the Vice-President acts as President.

nindian-polity-58-12.s: A ruling given by the Deputy Speaker while in the Chair:
o: can be appealed to the Speaker
must be ratified by the Speaker
cannot be appealed to the Speaker
can be appealed to the President
nindian-polity-58-12.x: While presiding, the Deputy Speaker has the Speaker's powers, and his rulings cannot be appealed to the Speaker.

nindian-polity-57-13.s: If both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are absent from a joint sitting of Parliament, it is presided over by the:
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
senior-most member of the Lok Sabha
nindian-polity-57-13.x: The Speaker presides over a joint sitting (Art. 118(4)), then the Deputy Speaker, then the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman.

n8fc688297c4.s: A resolution to remove the Speaker of the Lok Sabha requires advance notice of at least:
n8fc688297c4.x: Under Article 94 removal needs a majority of all the then members after 14 days' notice; the Speaker resigns to the Deputy Speaker.

nindian-polity-58-6.s: The date of election of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is fixed by the:
nindian-polity-58-6.x: The President fixes the Speaker's election date and the Speaker fixes the Deputy Speaker's.

n7bbd329f7bd.s: In which Lok Sabha did the office of Deputy Speaker remain vacant throughout?
n7bbd329f7bd.x: The Deputy Speaker's post remained vacant through the 17th Lok Sabha, and also through the 18th.

nindian-polity-57-37.s: Who appoints the Pro-Tem Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
nindian-polity-57-37.x: The President appoints the Pro-Tem Speaker; adjourning sine die, Tenth Schedule decisions and fixing the Deputy Speaker's election date are the Speaker's.

n6a1385ec964.s: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha addresses his resignation to the:
n6a1385ec964.x: The Deputy Chairman resigns to the Chairman and can be removed by an effective majority after 14 days' notice.

n26c1178800a.s: The six-month maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament is counted from:
o: the date of prorogation to the date of the next summons
the first sitting of one session to the first sitting of the next
the last sitting of one session to the first sitting of the next
the date of summons to the date of prorogation
n26c1178800a.x: The rule runs from the last sitting of one session to the first sitting of the next; the Budget, Monsoon and Winter names are only conventions.

n1eaeaaec92b.s: Which of the following is correct about the summoning of Parliament?
o: The President may summon the two Houses separately.
The Vice-President summons the Rajya Sabha.
Both Houses must always be summoned together.
n1eaeaaec92b.x: The President need not summon both Houses together, but each must meet within six months of its last sitting.

ne622f8dcf0f.s: Under which Article may the President send messages to either House of Parliament regarding a pending Bill?
ne622f8dcf0f.x: Article 86 lets the President address either or both Houses, require members' attendance and send messages on pending Bills.

n1adc5ef2690.s: The President's special address at the first session after each general election and the first session of each year is made under:
n1adc5ef2690.x: Article 87 provides for this special address; it is not required after every prorogation.

n4b133cccd9f.s: Who is usually appointed Speaker Pro Tem of a newly elected Lok Sabha?
o: The senior-most member of the House
n4b133cccd9f.x: The Speaker Pro Tem is the senior-most member, sworn in by the President; the outgoing Speaker only stays in office until just before the new House first meets.

n8e58d71e9da.s: Which of the following does NOT lapse on the prorogation of Parliament?
n8e58d71e9da.x: Bills do not lapse on prorogation, although pending notices generally lapse except notices to introduce bills.

nindian-polity-56-7.s: Removal of which of the following requires NO advance notice?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
nindian-polity-56-7.x: The President removes a Governor at pleasure without notice; the other three removals need 14 days' notice.

nindian-polity-58-14.s: While a resolution for his own removal is under consideration, the Deputy Speaker can:
nindian-polity-58-14.x: The Deputy Speaker cannot preside then but may speak, take part and vote in the first instance; no casting vote is allowed.

nindian-polity-57-11.s: Under which Article is the Speaker removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Lok Sabha?
nindian-polity-57-11.x: Article 94(c) requires an effective majority, after 14 days' notice; a simple majority is not enough.

nindian-polity-58-13.s: When not in the Chair, the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
o: can debate, move motions and vote in the first instance
can only give a casting vote
nindian-polity-58-13.x: Out of the Chair the Deputy Speaker is an ordinary member who can debate, move motions and vote in the first instance, unlike the Speaker.

nindian-polity-64-24.s: The lapse of pending bills on dissolution of the Lok Sabha is subject to the rules in:
nindian-polity-64-24.x: Dissolution ends the Lok Sabha and its pending business lapses, subject to Article 107; the Rajya Sabha is permanent.

nindian-polity-64-13.s: The President's power to dissolve the Lok Sabha is provided in:
nindian-polity-64-13.x: Article 85(2)(b) covers dissolution and 85(2)(a) prorogation; Article 123 is about ordinances.

nindian-polity-57-7.s: In normal sittings of the Lok Sabha, the Speaker:
o: votes in the first instance like any member
votes in the first instance and also has a casting vote
does not vote in the first instance but has a casting vote in a tie
nindian-polity-57-7.x: Under Article 100 the Speaker does not vote in the first instance but gives a casting vote when votes are tied.

nindian-polity-56-36.s: On assuming office, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha takes:
o: only the oath as a Member of Parliament
a separate oath administered by the President
a separate oath administered by the Chief Justice of India
a separate oath administered by the Pro-Tem Speaker
nindian-polity-56-36.x: The Speaker and Deputy Speaker take only the oath as MPs; there is no separate oath as presiding officer.

nindian-polity-64-6.s: The Budget, Monsoon and Winter sessions of Parliament are based on:
nindian-polity-64-6.x: The three-session pattern is a convention, and the Constitution prescribes no minimum number of sitting days.

nindian-polity-57-34.s: Who administers the oath to newly elected members of the Lok Sabha?
nindian-polity-57-34.x: The Pro-Tem Speaker swears in the new MPs and conducts the election of the regular Speaker.

nindian-polity-29-17.s: Under Rule 8(1), the date of the Deputy Speaker's election is fixed by the ____ and notified by the Secretary-General.
nindian-polity-29-17.x: The Speaker fixes the date of the Deputy Speaker's election and the Secretary-General notifies it to members.

nindian-polity-35-48.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Public Accounts Committee – scrutiny of public-sector undertaking accounts and commercial soundness
Estimates Committee – examination of budget estimates
Estimates Committee – suggesting economy in administration
Committee on Public Undertakings – scrutiny of PSU accounts
nindian-polity-35-48.x: The PAC scrutinises appropriation accounts and wasteful expenditure; PSU accounts are examined by the Committee on Public Undertakings.

nindian-polity-33-28.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: A Calling Attention Motion does not disrupt the scheduled daily agenda.
An Adjournment Motion interrupts normal parliamentary business.
A Calling Attention Motion involves censure of the Government.
An Adjournment Motion involves an element of censure of the Government.
nindian-polity-33-28.x: A Calling Attention Motion has no element of censure; it is the Adjournment Motion that implies censure.

n177b5de3d9f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the removal of the Speaker under Article 94(c)?
o: A notice of fourteen days is required.
The resolution needs only a simple majority of members present and voting.
The notice must be supported by at least fifty members.
The procedure is governed by Rules 200–203 of the Lok Sabha Rules of Procedure.
n177b5de3d9f.x: Removal needs a majority of all the then members of the House (an effective majority); a simple majority is not enough.

n837a4ff818f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about an Adjournment Motion?
o: The debate on it lasts not less than two hours and thirty minutes.
It needs the support of 50 members for admission.
It must relate to a single, definite matter of recent occurrence.
It can be moved in either House of Parliament.
n837a4ff818f.x: An Adjournment Motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.

n329b57a7249.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: A Censure Motion may be directed against a Minister, a group of Ministers or the whole Council.
A No-confidence Motion is directed against the entire Council of Ministers.
Passing a No-confidence Motion requires the Council of Ministers to resign.
Passing a Censure Motion compels the Council of Ministers to resign.
n329b57a7249.x: A passed Censure Motion does not compel resignation; a passed No-confidence Motion does.

nb5d06d384e1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Public Accounts Committee?
o: It has 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
A Minister can be a member of the Committee.
Its members are elected annually by PR-STV.
Its Chairperson is appointed by the Speaker.
nb5d06d384e1.x: Ministers cannot be members of the Public Accounts Committee.

n1773a432295.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ad hoc committees of Parliament?
o: Inquiry committees may be set up by a motion or by the Speaker or Chairman.
The Committee on MPLADS is an example of an inquiry committee.
Select and Joint Committees on Bills are ad hoc committees.
They continue permanently after completing their assigned task.
n1773a432295.x: Ad hoc committees end when their assigned task is completed.

nindian-polity-55-28.s: A privilege motion is referred to the:
nindian-polity-55-28.x: A privilege motion goes to the Committee of Privileges.

n6638803569e.s: After a resolution has been moved in Parliament, a resolution on the same subject is barred for:
n6638803569e.x: A resolution on the same subject is barred for one year; a resolution is always a substantive motion, must be put to vote, and cannot be withdrawn without the House's leave.

nindian-polity-33-11.s: Which device lets members raise urgent matters of public importance without prior notice?
nindian-polity-33-11.x: Zero Hour, an Indian innovation, is for raising urgent matters without notice; Question Hour is a formal procedure for questioning Ministers.

ncfb21291e09.s: In the Lok Sabha, a short-duration discussion without voting is held under:
ncfb21291e09.x: Rule 193 is a discussion without voting, Rule 184 a discussion followed by voting, and Rule 377 is for matters not raisable under any other device.

nindian-polity-55-4.s: A question that gets a written answer, with no supplementary questions allowed, is a:
nindian-polity-55-4.x: Unstarred questions get written answers without supplementaries; starred questions get oral answers with supplementaries.

n2dde54a6d12.s: The day-to-day proceedings of the Lok Sabha are governed mainly by the:
o: Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha
n2dde54a6d12.x: The Constitution gives only the broad framework; devices such as the No-Confidence Motion and Rule 377 come from the Rules of Procedure.

nindian-polity-33-2.s: Since 2014, the Rajya Sabha begins its day at 11 AM with:
nindian-polity-33-2.x: Since 2014 the Rajya Sabha has Zero Hour at 11 AM and Question Hour from noon to 1 PM; the Lok Sabha has Question Hour first.

na5c48fbdf31.s: Leave to move a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha requires the support of at least:
na5c48fbdf31.x: It needs 50 members' support; the motion is not expressly in the Constitution but flows from Article 75(3) and lies only in the Lok Sabha.

nindian-polity-55-6.s: A motion raised against a Minister for withholding or distorting facts is a:
nindian-polity-55-6.x: A privilege motion targets a Minister who withheld or distorted facts; a censure motion disapproves of specific policies.

nindian-polity-35-9.s: Which parliamentary committee regulates the timetable of the House's business?
nindian-polity-35-9.x: The Business Advisory Committee sets the timetable; the Rules Committee proposes rule changes and the Assurances Committee tracks Ministers' promises.

nindian-polity-34-16.s: At most how many starred questions are listed per day for oral answer?
nindian-polity-34-16.x: Starred questions are limited to 20 a day for oral answer; unstarred questions have no such limit.

nindian-polity-35-19.s: Ministers are barred from the PAC, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Petitions mainly because these committees:
o: consist only of Rajya Sabha members
meet only when Parliament is not in session
nindian-polity-35-19.x: These committees, along with COPU and the Subordinate Legislation Committee, scrutinise the government, so Ministers are kept out.

nc05098b9939.s: Inflation targeting at 4% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2% is associated with the committee headed by:
nc05098b9939.x: The Urjit Patel committee is linked with 4% ± 2% inflation targeting; Nachiket Mor is associated with financial inclusion and Shanta Kumar with FCI/PDS reform.

nf929b390acc.s: A resolution moved under a constitutional or statutory provision is called a:
nf929b390acc.x: Such a resolution is a statutory resolution; a Government resolution is one moved by a minister, e.g. to approve a treaty.

nindian-polity-55-18.s: Since 2015, the maximum number of matters that can be raised daily under Rule 377 is:
nindian-polity-55-18.x: Up to 30 matters a day can be raised under Rule 377 since 2015; Zero Hour lasts at most one hour.

nindian-polity-38-65.s: Which motion must state specific reasons for its adoption?
nindian-polity-38-65.x: A censure motion must state reasons; a no-confidence motion needs 50 members' support but no reasons, and the government moves a confidence motion.

n271a20f5d5b.s: Committees such as the PAC, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings are described as:
n271a20f5d5b.x: These committees, along with the Department-related Standing Committees, are described as watchdogs over the executive.

ndd1d2bd6b0c.s: Which is regarded as the most powerful weapon for enforcing the accountability of the executive?
ndd1d2bd6b0c.x: The no-confidence motion is the most powerful weapon of accountability and need not state reasons; Question Hour is the most effective day-to-day vigil.

n0f18645f3ea.s: The Public Accounts Committee was first set up in:
n0f18645f3ea.x: The PAC was set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919; it examines the CAG's audit reports.

nfc9af76f954.s: To raise a matter during Zero Hour, a member:
o: gives the same notice as for an ordinary question
intimates the Presiding Officer on the same day
needs the consent of the Minister concerned
nfc9af76f954.x: Zero Hour needs no ordinary-question notice; members intimate the Presiding Officer the same day, and it has no fixed duration in the Rules.

nindian-polity-55-48.s: A Confidence Motion can be moved in:
o: a joint sitting of both Houses
nindian-polity-55-48.x: Confidence motions are admissible only in the Lok Sabha.

n114ccea83eb.s: Defiance of a party Whip can attract disqualification under the:
n114ccea83eb.x: The Whip enforces attendance and voting on party lines, and defiance can attract disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.

nbfa9da20d73.s: The recommendations of the Public Accounts Committee are:
o: binding once approved by the Speaker
nbfa9da20d73.x: PAC recommendations are not binding; the PAC checks spending within the scope of the demand and examines execution, not policy.

nfff31d19856.s: Who rules on a point of order raised in the House?
nfff31d19856.x: A point of order, raised when proceedings depart from the Rules or the Constitution, is not debated; the Presiding Officer rules on it.

n47a26cd7bf3.s: Department-related Standing Committees (DRSCs) were set up in:
n47a26cd7bf3.x: DRSCs were set up in 1993; there are 24 (16 Lok Sabha and 8 Rajya Sabha), each with 31 members and a quorum of 11.

n7e10758a5d8.s: The Committee on Public Undertakings (1964) was created on the recommendation of the:
n7e10758a5d8.x: COPU came from the Krishna Menon Committee's recommendation; John Mathai's recommendation gave the Estimates Committee its present form in 1950.

nbeafecbc175.s: The short-duration discussion, an Indian parliamentary innovation, was introduced in:
nbeafecbc175.x: The short-duration discussion dates from 1953; it is limited to two hours and involves no vote.

nee7cf8fcba1.s: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is the ex-officio Chairperson of the:
nee7cf8fcba1.x: The Speaker is ex-officio Chairperson of the Business Advisory, Rules and General Purposes Committees.

nindian-polity-35-26.s: Since 1967, the Chairman of which committee has been appointed from the Opposition?
nindian-polity-35-26.x: The Speaker has appointed the PAC Chairman from the Opposition since 1967; the Estimates Committee Chairman comes from the ruling party.

nindian-polity-29-23.s: The form of closure in which all remaining clauses or demands are put to vote at once when the allotted time expires is called:
nindian-polity-29-23.x: The guillotine is the form of closure applied when the allotted time runs out, putting all remaining clauses or demands to vote at once.

nindian-polity-34-19.s: Which type of question deals with matters of urgent public importance?
nindian-polity-34-19.x: Short notice questions concern urgent matters; starred and unstarred questions concern matters of general public importance.

nindian-polity-29-6.s: Which of the following parliamentary devices is informal and not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure?
nindian-polity-29-6.x: Zero Hour, which follows Question Hour, is informal; Question Hour is formal and provided in the Rules.

nindian-polity-55-46.s: Asking and answering questions addressed to Ministers takes place during:
nindian-polity-55-46.x: Question Hour is for questions to Ministers; Zero Hour is informal and needs no notice.

nindian-polity-35-43.s: Consultative Committees of MPs for particular ministries are constituted by the:
nindian-polity-35-43.x: Consultative Committees are set up by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs and are not parliamentary committees in the strict sense.

nindian-polity-29-16.s: A matter that cannot be raised through questions, calling attention or other motions is raised in the Lok Sabha under:
nindian-polity-29-16.x: Rule 377 covers such matters; it requires written notice and the Speaker's consent.

nindian-polity-55-3.s: Question Hour, supplementary questions and adjournment motions together are described as the:
nindian-polity-55-3.x: Together they let Parliament question the government, follow up and raise urgent matters, forming the 'accountability triangle'.

n139c0d59bc1.s: In which year was the Calling Attention device introduced?
n139c0d59bc1.x: Calling Attention dates from 1954; the short-duration discussion is from 1953 and Zero Hour is associated with 1962.

nindian-polity-21-32.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
nindian-polity-21-32.x: Article 113 deals with Demands for Grants; the Appropriation Bill is under Article 114.

n3c07f83dcfd.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the role of the Rajya Sabha on a Money Bill?
o: It must return the Bill within 14 days, with or without recommendations.
If not returned within 14 days, the Bill is deemed passed by both Houses.
The Lok Sabha may accept or reject the Rajya Sabha's recommendations.
A deadlock over a Money Bill can be resolved through a joint sitting.
n3c07f83dcfd.x: There is no joint sitting for a Money Bill (Article 109 governs it).

n9403271632d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about timelines for assent to State Bills?
o: The April 2025 Tamil Nadu Governor judgment laid down fixed timelines for Governors.
In November 2025, a five-judge Bench advised on a Presidential Reference that courts cannot fix such timelines.
The November 2025 opinion upheld the deemed assent granted in the Tamil Nadu case.
n9403271632d.x: The November 2025 advisory opinion held that courts cannot fix timelines or declare deemed assent, so it did not uphold the Tamil Nadu deemed assent.

nca8233bdb2a.s: Which of the following is NOT an option available to the Governor under Article 200?
o: Assenting to a Bill passed by the State Legislature
Reserving a Bill for the consideration of the President
Returning a Money Bill for reconsideration
nca8233bdb2a.x: The Governor cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration.

n5f6fa40573b.s:
Assertion (A): Adjournment sine die causes all Bills pending before the House to lapse.
Reason (R): Dissolution of the Lok Sabha causes all pending business before it to lapse.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n5f6fa40573b.x: Adjournment or adjournment sine die does not make Bills lapse; only dissolution makes all pending Lok Sabha business lapse.

nd97f4234d7a.s: On dissolution of the Lok Sabha, which of the following Bills lapses?
o: A Bill passed by the Lok Sabha but pending in the Rajya Sabha
A Bill passed by both Houses and awaiting the President's assent
A Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha that the Lok Sabha has not passed
A Bill returned by the President for reconsideration
nd97f4234d7a.x: A Bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses; the other three survive dissolution.

nindian-polity-21-16.s: Under Article 110(2), a Bill is NOT a Money Bill merely because it deals with:
nindian-polity-21-16.x: A Bill only about fines or penalties is not a Money Bill; taxes, borrowing and the Consolidated Fund are Money Bill matters.

n660eac43b34.s: In counting the six-month period for a joint sitting under Article 108, adjournments of more than ____ consecutive days are excluded.
n660eac43b34.x: Periods of prorogation and adjournment over four consecutive days are excluded; rejection or final disagreement on amendments are the other grounds.

n9b3d69c93d5.s: In the Lok Sabha, time for Private Members' Bills is allotted by the:
o: Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions
n9b3d69c93d5.x: The Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions allots the time; defeat of such a Bill has no bearing on the government.

n6ce1fac92b8.s: Under Article 110(3), the final decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill rests with the:
n6ce1fac92b8.x: The Speaker's decision is final, and the certificate is endorsed on the Bill sent to the Rajya Sabha and presented to the President.

n0dfbd6cd4ba.s: In the Rajya Sabha, time for Private Members' Bills is allotted by its:
o: Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions
n0dfbd6cd4ba.x: The Rajya Sabha has no Committee on Private Members' Bills; its Business Advisory Committee allots the time.

n82b8b21117b.s: A Financial Bill-I under Article 117(1) can be introduced:
n82b8b21117b.x: It is introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the President's recommendation; the Rajya Sabha may amend or reject it.

n78bfe102e18.s: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 on simultaneous elections proposes a new Article:
n78bfe102e18.x: The Bill proposes Article 82A; it remained before the Joint Parliamentary Committee and has not been enacted.

n345a8c60a00.s: Clause-by-clause consideration of a Bill takes place during the:
n345a8c60a00.x: The Second Reading covers general discussion, committee stage and clause-by-clause voting; the Third Reading concerns the Bill as a whole.

n44dcd1f263e.s: The joint sitting of Parliament in 2002 was held on the:
n44dcd1f263e.x: Joint sittings were held in 1961 (Dowry Prohibition), 1978 (Banking Service Commission Repeal) and 2002 (Prevention of Terrorism).

n6a53e868919.s: The Bill that gives effect to the tax proposals of the Budget is the:
n6a53e868919.x: The Finance Bill gives effect to the Budget's tax proposals; every Money Bill is a Financial Bill, but not every Financial Bill is a Money Bill.

nindian-polity-21-6.s: On dissolution of the Lok Sabha, a Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha that the Lok Sabha has never passed:
o: goes automatically to a joint sitting
nindian-polity-21-6.x: Such a Bill survives dissolution, while Bills pending in the Lok Sabha or passed by it and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapse; prorogation ends no Bill.

n3ef95e177f6.s: Can a joint sitting be summoned for a Bill that has lapsed on dissolution of the Lok Sabha?
o: Yes, within six months of dissolution
No, a joint sitting cannot be held for a lapsed Bill
Yes, if the Rajya Sabha so requests
n3ef95e177f6.x: A joint sitting cannot be summoned for a Bill that has already lapsed; dissolution can end the Bill before the deadlock procedure operates.

nindian-polity-61-12.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: President – emoluments and office expenses charged on the CFI
Supreme Court Judges – salary, allowances and pension charged on the CFI
High Court Judges – salary, allowances and pension charged on the CFI
Prime Minister and Union Ministers – salaries and allowances are votable
nindian-polity-61-12.x: High Court judges' salaries are charged on the State's Consolidated Fund; only their pensions are charged on the CFI.

nf6633d14a8d.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Supplementary grant – sanctioned amount is insufficient
Additional grant – sanctioned amount is insufficient
Excess grant – expenditure exceeds the amount already granted
Vote of credit – unexpected demand of indefinite magnitude or character
nf6633d14a8d.x: An additional grant covers a new service not included in the Budget; insufficiency is met by a supplementary grant.

n572917a8966.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Contingency Fund of India?
o: It is provided for under Article 267.
It was established by the Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950.
It is held by the Finance Secretary in the Department of Expenditure.
It is at the President's disposal for unforeseen expenditure pending Parliament's approval.
n572917a8966.x: The Fund is held by the Finance Secretary in the Department of Economic Affairs, not the Department of Expenditure.

nindian-polity-79-15.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 112(3) – charged expenditure on the CFI
Article 114(3) – Appropriation Act for withdrawal from the CFI
Article 125 – salaries and allowances of High Court Judges
Article 221 – salaries and allowances of High Court Judges
nindian-polity-79-15.x: Article 125 covers Supreme Court judges' salaries; High Court judges' pay is under Article 221.

ncca12304447.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Public Account of India?
o: Provident funds held in a fiduciary capacity are credited to it.
Small savings are credited to it.
Deposits and remittances are included in it.
Every withdrawal from it requires an appropriation law.
ncca12304447.x: Withdrawal from the Public Account does not need appropriation the way withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund does.

n9b5ea742f87.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a vote on account?
o: It is an advance for part of the year, generally about two months, until the Appropriation Act is passed.
In election years it may cover three to five months.
Since the Budget moved to 1 February (2017), it is needed in every regular Budget year.
n9b5ea742f87.x: Since the 1 February Budget, a vote on account is usually needed only in interim-Budget years.

ndda57110f03.s: An amendment to the Appropriation Bill that varies the amount of expenditure charged on the CFI is:
o: permitted in the Lok Sabha only
ndda57110f03.x: No amendment may vary a voted grant or charged expenditure; the Appropriation Bill also carries an automatic repeal clause.

nindian-polity-61-34.s: Which Article provides for the vote on account, votes of credit and exceptional grants?
nindian-polity-61-34.x: Article 116 covers these; 112 is the Annual Financial Statement, 113 the estimates procedure and 115 supplementary, additional or excess grants.

nindian-polity-61-37.s: The salaries and allowances of High Court Judges are charged on the:
nindian-polity-61-37.x: High Court judges' salaries are charged on the State's Consolidated Fund; the President's emoluments, Supreme Court judges' pay and debt charges are charged on the CFI.

n000130c706b.s: Which of the following forms part of the Consolidated Fund of India?
o: Treasury Bills raised by the Union Government
n000130c706b.x: The CFI comprises Union revenues, loans raised (including Treasury Bills) and loan repayments; provident funds, small savings and remittances go to the Public Account.

n9ef79b1e4fb.s: The Constitution refers to the Union Budget as the:
n9ef79b1e4fb.x: Article 112 uses 'Annual Financial Statement'; the word 'Budget' does not occur in the Constitution.

nindian-polity-79-18.s: Whose salary, pension and office expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
nindian-polity-79-18.x: The CAG's costs are charged; the Vice-President as such (paid as Rajya Sabha Chairman), Ministers and the Election Commission are not.

n47d67ba747a.s: The Union Budget is presented in two parts, namely the:
n47d67ba747a.x: The Budget covers the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account and is presented in Revenue and Capital parts.

nindian-polity-61-11.s: Under which Article is the Public Account of India constituted?
nindian-polity-61-11.x: The Public Account is under Article 266(2); the Consolidated Fund is under 266(1) and the Contingency Fund under 267(1).

nindian-polity-38-11.s: A token cut reduces a demand for grant by:
nindian-polity-38-11.x: A token cut reduces a demand by ₹100; a policy cut reduces it to ₹1 and an economy cut by a specified amount.

n9cc44d2fc3c.s: Cut motions are moved in the Lok Sabha during:
o: the general discussion on the Budget
n9cc44d2fc3c.x: Cut motions are moved only in the Lok Sabha during voting on Demands for Grants; if passed, they signal loss of confidence.

nindian-polity-61-40.s: Savings bank deposits held by the Government in trust are credited to the:
nindian-polity-61-40.x: Savings bank deposits are held in trust in the Public Account; treasury bills, market loans and foreign loans go to the CFI.

n958561072cb.s: The Budget process begins with the issue of the Budget Circular, generally in:
n958561072cb.x: The Budget Circular is generally issued in September, and printing of Budget documents is marked by the Halwa ceremony.

n69aedb76c4a.s: Who presented the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 on 14 February 2026?
n69aedb76c4a.x: Finance Minister Payyavula Keshav presented the main Budget; K. Atchannaidu presented the separate agriculture budget.

nindian-polity-61-15.s: The pensions of High Court Judges are charged on the:
nindian-polity-61-15.x: High Court judges' pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, not the State's.

nindian-polity-79-14.s: Under which Article does Parliament fix by law the salaries of the Speaker and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
nindian-polity-79-14.x: Under Article 97 Parliament fixes the salaries of the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman and Deputy Chairman, charged on the CFI.

nindian-polity-79-37.s: Which provision requires an Appropriation Act for every withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India, even for charged expenditure?
nindian-polity-79-37.x: Article 114(3) requires an Appropriation Act for every withdrawal, so even charged expenditure, which is not voted, needs one.

nindian-polity-61-8.s: Money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India only on the authority of:
o: an appropriation law passed by Parliament
nindian-polity-61-8.x: The President cannot withdraw money alone; Article 114 requires a law of Parliament (the Appropriation Act).

nindian-polity-61-9.s: Executive disbursements from the Public Account of India:
o: need no prior vote of Parliament
need the approval of the Rajya Sabha
need a joint sitting of Parliament
nindian-polity-61-9.x: The government runs the Public Account as a banker for money held in trust, so payments need no prior vote of Parliament.

nindian-polity-35-47.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Parliamentary Committees – broadly classified into Standing and Ad-hoc Committees
Financial Committees – examples of Standing Committees
Department-Related Standing Committees – Standing Committees dealing with departments
Inquiry Committees – examples of Standing Committees
nindian-polity-35-47.x: Inquiry committees are ad hoc committees, not standing committees.

n6863c4e6097.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Public Accounts Committee?
o: It may take up certain matters on its own.
It tests efficiency, economy and propriety, not merely legality.
It examines the audit reports of the CAG.
It can examine the formulation of policy itself.
n6863c4e6097.x: The PAC examines only the execution of policy, not policy as such; its recommendations are also not binding.

n0f795b0ba9d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs)?
o: Each DRSC has 31 members: 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.
There are 24 DRSCs: 16 under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha.
The quorum of a DRSC is 15.
Ministers are ineligible to be members.
n0f795b0ba9d.x: The quorum of a DRSC is 11, not 15.

nfc060b58296.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Bills before parliamentary committees?
o: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 on One Nation, One Election is before a JPC.
The FCRA (Amendment) Bill, 2026 is before a JPC.
The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 proposes a new Article 82A.
The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhisthan Bill, 2025 is before a Select Committee of the Rajya Sabha alone.
nfc060b58296.x: The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhisthan Bill, 2025 is also before a JPC (a joint committee of both Houses), not a single-House Select Committee.

n24a19799320.s: The Estimates Committee, the largest financial committee of Parliament, consists of:
o: 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
30 members: 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
31 members: 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
n24a19799320.x: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha, with a chairman from the ruling party; the PAC has 22 (15 LS + 7 RS).

n271afb2831b.s: The term of office of members of the financial committees of Parliament is:
n271afb2831b.x: Members are elected annually by PR-STV for a one-year term; Ministers are ineligible.

nea72838b731.s: Which parliamentary committee suggests economies and alternative policies?
nea72838b731.x: The Estimates Committee suggests economies and alternative policies; the PAC is the watchdog on departmental expenditure and irregularities.

n24daf1ebf86.s: Which parliamentary committee examines the reports of the National Commissions for SCs and STs?
o: Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs
n24daf1ebf86.x: The Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs examines welfare programmes and the National Commissions' reports; Ministers cannot serve on it.

n169693f8ab4.s: In which year did a Joint Parliamentary Committee investigate the Harshad Mehta securities scam?
n169693f8ab4.x: JPCs probed Bofors (1987), Harshad Mehta (1992), Ketan Parekh (2001), soft-drink pesticides (2003) and 2G spectrum (2011).

n338d6f543d9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about anti-defection case law?
o: G. Viswanathan: an expelled member continues to belong to the original party for Tenth Schedule purposes.
G. Viswanathan: an expelled member who joins another party may be treated as having voluntarily given up membership.
G. Viswanathan: expulsion automatically protects a member from disqualification for joining another party.
Ravi S. Naik: voluntarily giving up membership may be inferred from conduct.
n338d6f543d9.x: Expulsion gives no such protection; an expelled member who joins another party may be disqualified for voluntarily giving up membership.

nindian-polity-77-9.s: Under the Tenth Schedule, which pair of member category and disqualification trigger is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Party-elected member – votes or abstains contrary to the party whip without prior permission
Independent elected member – joins a political party only after six months from taking the seat
Nominated member – joins a political party after six months from taking the seat
Presiding Officer – joins another political party while holding or after vacating office
nindian-polity-77-9.x: An independent member is disqualified for joining any political party after election; the six-month window applies only to nominated members.

n9d162d1c145.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Keisham Meghachandra Singh v. Speaker, Manipur?
o: Disqualification petitions are ordinarily to be decided within three months.
The three-month period admits exceptions in extraordinary cases.
The Court asked Parliament to consider replacing the Speaker with a permanent independent tribunal.
The judgment transferred all Tenth Schedule decisions to the Election Commission.
n9d162d1c145.x: The Court did not transfer Tenth Schedule decisions to the Election Commission; it only suggested considering an independent tribunal.

nindian-polity-77-16.s: Which pair of disqualification case and deciding authority is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Defection disqualification of an MP – Speaker or Chairman of the House concerned
General disqualification of a Union MP – Speaker or Chairman of the House concerned
General disqualification of a State MLA or MLC – Governor of the State
Defection disqualification of a State legislator – presiding officer of the State House concerned
nindian-polity-77-16.x: General (non-defection) disqualification of an MP is decided by the President, not the presiding officer.

n084a4ef79da.s: Which pair of case and holding is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Ravi S. Naik v. Union of India – voluntarily giving up membership may be inferred from conduct
G. Viswanathan v. Speaker, Tamil Nadu – expelled member continues to belong to the party
Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu – upheld the validity of the Tenth Schedule
Subhash Desai v. Principal Secretary, Governor of Maharashtra – expelled member continues to belong to the party
n084a4ef79da.x: Subhash Desai held that the political party appoints the whip and the leader in the House; the expelled-member holding is G. Viswanathan.

nindian-polity-77-36.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about general (non-defection) disqualification of legislators?
o: The President decides the question for a Union MP.
The Governor decides the question for a State MLA or MLC.
The ECI's opinion is mandatory and binding in the case of an MP.
The ECI's opinion is non-binding in the case of a State legislator.
nindian-polity-77-36.x: For both MPs and State legislators the ECI's opinion is compulsory and binding.

nc1c63fcb102.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992)?
o: It was decided by a Constitution Bench.
It upheld the constitutional validity of the Tenth Schedule.
It struck down Paragraph 7 of the Schedule.
It held that the Tenth Schedule violates the basic structure by restricting legislators' freedom of speech.
nc1c63fcb102.x: The Court held that the law did not violate legislators' freedom of speech or the basic structure.

ncefe1a3f748.s:
Assertion (A): The Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) recommended disqualification only for voluntarily giving up membership or defying the whip on a confidence or no-confidence motion.
Reason (R): The Law Commission's 170th Report (1999) recommended deleting the split and merger exceptions.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ncefe1a3f748.x: Both describe real recommendations of different bodies; a later Law Commission report cannot explain the Goswami Committee's earlier proposal.

n19bb1a739ec.s: According to the Subhash Desai judgment, the whip of a party in the House is appointed by the:
n19bb1a739ec.x: The legislature party cannot be conflated with the political party, and it is the political party that appoints the whip.

nca34fa8cf81.s: The original Tenth Schedule, concerning Sikkim's association with India, was added by the:
nca34fa8cf81.x: The 35th Amendment introduced a Sikkim-related Tenth Schedule, which the 36th Amendment omitted; it was not the anti-defection Schedule.

n056842331cd.s: While deciding a disqualification question under the Tenth Schedule, the Speaker or Chairman acts as a:
n056842331cd.x: The presiding officer acts as a tribunal, subject to limited judicial review; the ECI gives no opinion here (that applies under Articles 103 and 192).

nd7a359c563f.s: In the Karnataka defection case (2019), the Supreme Court upheld the disqualification of how many rebel MLAs?
nd7a359c563f.x: The Court upheld the disqualification of 17 rebel MLAs but held the Speaker could not bar them from contesting till the end of the term.

nindian-polity-77-4.s: Which Article deals with disqualifications for membership of a State Legislature?
nindian-polity-77-4.x: Article 191 covers State disqualifications and 190 State vacation of seats; Articles 101 and 102 are the Parliament counterparts.

n3b201d518b1.s: The 'one-third split' exception under the Tenth Schedule was deleted by the:
n3b201d518b1.x: The 91st Amendment (2003) deleted the split exception; only the Para 4 merger exception remains.

n2d89753a432.s: The expression 'Aaya Ram Gaya Ram' became associated with defections in which State in 1967?
n2d89753a432.x: The phrase comes from Haryana, 1967; the Y.B. Chavan Committee studied defections in 1967-69, and the law came with the 52nd Amendment, 1985.

na90291b157e.s: In a breach of privilege case, the final decision on action against the offender is taken by the:
na90291b157e.x: The Committee of Privileges examines and recommends, but the House takes the final decision.

nindian-polity-77-12.s: The Anti-Defection Law (52nd Amendment) came into force on:
nindian-polity-77-12.x: The 52nd Amendment received assent on 15 February 1985 and took effect on 1 March 1985.
